newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent sets soft North Sea tone as margins ease.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent sets soft North Sea tone as margins ease.

text.p: Cash Brent eased in early talk on Tuesday as outright paper values and intermonth spreads softened against a background of poor refining margins, traders said.

July Brent shed 25 cents to trade at $19.75 a barrel on the IPE and 15-day forward paper spreads were also easier, June/July talked at +4/+8 cents from trade on Friday at +8/+9 cents. July/August lost a cent or two to talk at -5/-2 cents.
"It's been a typically slow start this morning but if anything the market feels under pressure," said a trader.
Poor margins throughout Europe and slack demand were depressing sentiment, he said.
Returns for a typical Rotterdam refinery cracking Brent crude began the week at about $1.12 a barrel, down from last week's already depressed average of $1.23.
Hydroskimming yields fell to a negative 30 cents a barrel from an average loss of 17 cents last week.
Brent Contracts for Difference (CFDs) for May 27-30, which jumped to around July Brent +5/+10 cents on Friday after a Dated Brent deal at July +17 cents, slipped to +3/+8 cents.
Dealers said the prompt backwardation on the CFD market was expected to be short-lived. Next week (June 2-6) was talked at July Brent -18 cents.
Only one Brent cargo was due to be nominated June 11-13 loading dates on Tuesday, traders said.
Other North Sea crudes were notionally unchanged in thin activity.

June cargoes of Statfjord and Oseberg traded on Friday, but the deals gave little indication on market direction. The details of the first were kept private and the second was done on a quotes-related basis.
